target_customer: Space industry operators needing megawatt-scale orbital power for manufacturing, data centers, defense and propulsion
problem: Space operations are power-starved, and solar is costly at megawatt scale; the company proposes in-orbit fusion power using the vacuum of space for plasma confinement.
business_model: Develop a megawatt-class in-orbit fusion power source and sell power to space customers (pre-revenue)

founders.name: Edward Hinson
education: PhD in nuclear engineering and engineering physics, University of Wisconsin-Madison
founders.background_notes: YC page cites 20+ years in plasma modeling and experimental plasma physics.

founders.name: Galen Burke
education: PhD in nuclear engineering and engineering physics (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page cites 15+ years in diagnostics and plasma physics.

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires a levitated dipole fusion reactor with high-temperature superconducting magnets operating in orbit; no flight hardware existed and net-energy fusion is unproven.

defensibility.rationale: Deep plasma physics expertise and hardware barriers make copying hard, though the dipole concept itself is old (proposed decades earlier).

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No well resourced player was found building in-orbit fusion at founding; ground fusion firms exist but do not target space.

market_need_then: Launch costs had fallen roughly tenfold over a decade per the company's pitch, and growing interest in orbital data centers and manufacturing created demand for large amounts of power in space.

identity.logo: logo file offered in a media assets section, design not described
identity.voice_and_tone: Physics-led and ambitious, framing space as power-starved

branding.community_and_virality: No community or merch found; an investor (Tekedia Capital) wrote a post announcing its investment.

brand_strength.rationale: Zephyr (a gentle wind) is an evocative real word, but common and unrelated to fusion, with little evidence of brand pull.

outcome_analysis: Zephyr Fusion is an active Fall 2025 deep tech company led by two plasma physicists with national lab and Wisconsin backgrounds, pursuing in-orbit dipole fusion. Funding is small and mostly aggregator reported, with an investor post from Tekedia Capital in May 2026. The technical risk is extreme and no hardware has flown, so any outcome is a long dated bet.
notes: Aggregators (VCBacked, PitchBook, FundedIQ) report about 500K total, labeled pre-seed or seed, with a November 2025 extension from Pioneer Fund, Brimstone Hill Capital, Spot VC and Syntax Ventures; all unverified and not recorded as rounds. The Tekedia round stage is not stated by the source, so recorded as other with no amount; the post is the investor's own announcement dated 2026-05-22. Competitor list empty because no in-orbit fusion competitor dated near the batch was found; the orbital power companies seen (Mantis Space, Space Power) do different things. One directory lists founding as 2023, conflicting with YC page (2025). Name origin not found.
